title: Reformation targets $1B valuation with IPO
gist: Reformation is pursuing an IPO targeting up to $1B valuation, pricing 14M+ shares at $15–$17, expecting ~$134.5M in net proceeds mostly used to repay debt. The brand posted $507M revenue and $12.6M net income in 2025, with over 30% of new DTC shoppers acquired through physical retail stores.

title: Zalando invests in AI robotics
gist: Zalando has taken an investment stake in German AI robotics firm Sereact to accelerate logistics automation, with a focus on returns processing.

title: German ecommerce increases 4.3% in first half 2026
gist: German e-commerce turnover grew 4.3% in H1 2026 year-over-year, accelerating to 5.1% growth in Q2, suggesting recovering consumer confidence in one of Europe's largest online markets.

title: Why brands like Untuckit are experimenting with robot-made T-shirts
gist: Some U.S. apparel brands, including Untuckit, are experimenting with AI-powered robotics to enable domestic manufacturing, as tariffs have so far failed to shift import patterns away from Asian countries.

title: GameStop discloses 10% eBay stake as it pushes for a deal
gist: GameStop has doubled its eBay stake to nearly 10% after eBay rejected its $56B acquisition bid in May, with CEO Ryan Cohen publicly signaling he will pursue the deal with or without board cooperation.

title: AliExpress hit with record $625M fine after failing to make EU-ordered fixes
gist: The European Commission fined AliExpress over $625M under the Digital Services Act — the largest DSA fine to date — for failing to adequately remove illegal, unsafe, and counterfeit products from its platform.

title: American Eagle is turning RushTok and malls into its back-to-school sales engine
gist: American Eagle's 2026 back-to-school campaign spans ~10 weeks with mall events, campus partnerships, and multiple talent deals including Sydney Sweeney and World Cup winner Lamine Yamal, deliberately moving away from a single monoculture campaign after last year's Sweeney push brought in 790,000 new customers.

title: Exclusive: Target aims to strengthen its tween business with new multi-year Pacsun partnership
gist: Target is launching a multi-year, 100+ style tween apparel line co-created with Pacsun, priced under $30, available monthly in stores and on Target.com — framed as a deeper, longer-term brand partnership than Target's typical limited collaborations.

title: Advertise in ChatGPT
gist: OpenAI has launched an advertising platform, ads.openai.com, opening ChatGPT to paid advertising placements.

title: Unpacked: How agentic AI is reshaping the consumer journey
gist: A sponsored Glossy guide argues that agentic AI is moving from concept to deployment in commerce, with Bain projecting agentic AI could represent 15–25% of total U.S. e-commerce by 2030 as platforms like Google and OpenAI embed agents into shopping flows.

title: Allegro Group GMV increases 14%
gist: Polish marketplace Allegro reported 13.7% GMV growth in H1 vs. the same period in 2025, with international GMV up 64.8%.

title: Brands Briefing: Why employee-generated content is a priority for brands like Starbucks and Mephisto
gist: Brands including Starbucks and Mephisto are making employee-generated content a deliberate strategy, with Mephisto USA explicitly hiring store staff who can also create daily social content and act as affiliates.

title: More brands are leaning on founders to drive social content
gist: Founder-led short-form video content is becoming an informal requirement for DTC brands, with retailers reportedly factoring a founder's social presence into wholesale decisions because it can drive in-store traffic.

title: Fashion Briefing: Canadian brands are investing in US fulfillment centers in wake of new tariffs
gist: Canadian apparel brands are accelerating investment in US-based fulfillment centers to sidestep new Trump tariffs, but the cost of local fulfillment is proving significant.

title: Kroger’s new CEO, a Walmart veteran, is focused on speed and execution
gist: Kroger's new CEO Greg Foran, a Walmart veteran, is emphasizing speed, execution, and financial discipline, with an early move being the $1.7B acquisition of Giant Eagle.

title: The back-to-school denim wars are starting earlier and lasting longer
gist: Major retailers including Pacsun, Kohl's, and Hollister are launching back-to-school denim campaigns earlier than ever, as NRF data shows 62% of shoppers had already started back-to-school shopping by early July, up from 55% in 2024.

title: Nike resets online distribution in ‘fragmented’ China market
gist: Nike is consolidating its China online presence from over 1,000 digital storefronts down to a handful of official channels on Tmall, JD.com, and Douyin, cutting major wholesale distributors from online sales amid a 12% revenue decline in the region.

title: New Ecommerce Tools: July 22, 2026
gist: This week's e-commerce tool roundup covers new launches including Squarespace drop-selling features, a DoorDash–Shopify integration for on-demand delivery, TikTok Shop's managed services pilot, and Dotdigital's AI loyalty platform.

title: 54% of shoppers report more shelf gaps since the start of Middle East conflict
gist: Research from invent.ai found that 54% of UK shoppers report worse on-shelf availability since Middle East conflict began, with 40% of planned grocery spend unavailable on average, and fashion shoppers particularly quick to switch brands or channels when facing stockouts.

title: Michaels says Google-powered AI assistant doubles conversion rate of traditional search
gist: Michaels' AI shopping assistant 'Ask Mike', built on Google Cloud's Gemini platform, has logged 75,000 conversations since its quiet May launch and reportedly doubles the conversion rate compared to traditional on-site search.

title: Michaels launches AI shopping assistant
gist: Michaels launched 'Ask Mike', an AI shopping assistant built with Google Cloud's Gemini platform in six weeks, offering personalized product recommendations and creative guidance, with plans to add AI-generated product overviews and contextual prompts.

title: How the shifting shopping calendar has become a customer acquisition opportunity
gist: Traditional retail peaks like Prime Day, Black Friday, and back-to-school have stretched into multi-week or multi-month events, reshaping how brands compete for customer acquisition across an increasingly elongated shopping calendar.

title: Marketplace Briefing: How Whatnot’s AI-powered recommendation system gives it a competitive edge
gist: Whatnot has reduced recommendation latency to minutes, allowing its system to ingest real-time signals like sold-out inventory from active livestreams and immediately adjust what products it surfaces to buyers.

title: What to know about new proposed tariffs on Canadian goods
gist: The Trump administration announced new tariffs on Canadian goods — covering autos, dairy, alcohol, and select consumer categories — set to take effect August 19, though negotiations could alter final rates before then.

title: Tractor Supply sputters in Q2, lowers outlook
gist: Tractor Supply posted a Q2 comp decline of 1.5% and cut its full-year outlook, citing drought, discretionary pullback, and encroachment by Amazon and Walmart into its rural customer base.

title: Google quietly gives ground on PMax controls
gist: Google is testing a feature that lets media buyers exclude third-party search partners and the Google Display Network from Performance Max campaigns, offering more spending control than the product has historically allowed.

title: How Best Buy is rethinking retail footprints for AI products like Ray-Ban Meta glasses
gist: Best Buy is rolling out 30x30-foot Meta AI shop-in-shop displays in select stores as part of its partnership to sell Ray-Ban Meta glasses, rethinking how experiential retail works for AI hardware.

title: Is Hoka slowing down?
gist: Deckers Brands posted Q1 revenue above $1 billion for the first time, with Hoka up 8% and DTC sales leading at +17%, though growth is projected below analyst expectations for the full year, raising questions about whether the brand's peak momentum has passed.

title: Ross accelerates brick-and-mortar expansion with nearly 50 new locations
gist: Ross Stores is opening 47 new locations in June–July 2026 as part of a plan to launch around 110 stores this year, riding strong traffic growth and benefiting from consumers trading down to off-price retail.

title: Hanes embraces risqué marketing in creative shakeup for basics brand
gist: Hanes launched a risqué, confidence-themed campaign called 'Get Comfortable' across social, OOH, and online video, marking a deliberate creative pivot following its $2.2 billion acquisition by Gildan Activewear.

title: Monday.com is the latest tech company to blame AI for layoffs — here are 20 others
gist: Monday.com is cutting 20% of its workforce (600+ employees) citing an AI-driven restructuring, joining a wave of tech companies — including Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, and Oracle — that have collectively eliminated nearly 140,000 jobs in 2026 while attributing cuts to AI transformation. FT analysis found companies naming AI as a layoff factor have underperformed the Nasdaq by ~10% in the 30 days after announcements, suggesting market skepticism.

title: What is happening to jobs? Separating AI hype from reality
gist: A Stanford SIEPR research brief finds that AI's measurable impact on aggregate employment remains small so far, with the clearest negative effect being reduced hiring of entry-level and recent-graduate workers in AI-exposed roles; productivity gains from AI tools are real but concentrated among less-experienced workers, and firm adoption remains uneven with most companies still in the experimentation phase.

title: Cloudflare's new AI traffic options for customers
gist: Cloudflare is expanding its AI traffic controls for all customers, introducing granular blocking options across three bot categories — Search, Agent, and Training — with Training and Agent bots to be blocked by default on ad-displaying pages for new domains from September 15, 2026. The update also adds a BotBase directory for enterprise customers, a content-use signal for robots.txt, and a transitive trust framework for agentic traffic.

title: Retail brands risk optimizing the wrong thing
gist: The share of digital commerce journeys starting on a brand's own website dropped from 82% in 2014 to 38% by 2024, with AI platforms increasingly capturing early purchase intent before shoppers ever reach a retailer's owned properties. Brands optimizing only for on-site experience risk being absent from AI-generated shortlists that now shape consideration sets upstream.

title: Mythbusters: AI visibility’s biggest misconceptions
gist: An estimated 30% of shoppers now use AI tools for product research, up from 12% a year ago, and brands are racing to understand how they appear in LLM-generated results — but experts say common AIO strategies are built on misconceptions.

title: N.Y. Targets AI Models in Product Ads
gist: New York State now requires clear disclosures when product ads contain AI-generated images of people, and Amazon has already directed third-party sellers to flag such content before uploading — a compliance burden that falls hardest on smaller merchants. Critics argue the law disproportionately penalizes affordable AI-generated imagery while leaving expensive but heavily manipulated traditional photography largely untouched.

title: Online retail sales surge in the United Kingdom
gist: UK online retail sales rose 11.7% year-on-year in Q2, with June up 14.4%, pushing the online share of total retail to its highest point since April 2021.

title: The new rules of cross-border commerce after de minimis
gist: Since July 1, the EU's de minimis exemption is gone: every parcel now incurs customs duty regardless of value, with a €3 per-line-item charge on shipments under €150, and the merchant — not the carrier or customer — is legally liable.

title: Stressed parents turn to BNPL for back-to-school shopping
gist: A survey of 1,075 U.S. consumers found 45% of households plan to use BNPL for back-to-school purchases this year, up from 39% in 2025, with financial stress and tight household budgets cited as the main drivers.

title: Modern Retail+ Research: Brands are expanding their creator marketing strategies
gist: A survey of 125 brand and agency professionals finds marketers are using creator partnerships beyond awareness, now tapping influencers for seasonal campaigns, product launches, and product development.

title: Google’s AI search is rapidly becoming the default, new data shows
gist: Google's AI Overviews now appear in 43% of searches, up from 15% a year ago, with AI Mode visits more than doubling — turning Google increasingly into a destination rather than a traffic source for publishers and retailers.

title: New Ecommerce Tools: July 29, 2026
gist: Practical Ecommerce rounds up new merchant tools for the week of July 29, 2026, covering logistics, search, payments, post-purchase, chargeback prevention, and AI-powered commerce integrations from providers including Algolia, Shopify, Amazon Business, and ESW.

title: Rushden Car Accessories Seller Accelerates Warehouse Expansion and Headcount After Surging Orders
gist: UK automotive accessories seller Blillov moved into a warehouse nine times larger than its previous site six months ahead of schedule after adding Temu as a sales channel, which quickly grew to about one-fifth of total turnover and brought in a distinct customer base.

title: PopSockets’ next act hinges on DTC, TikTok and a bigger product ecosystem
gist: PopSockets is rebuilding its growth strategy around limited-edition drops, TikTok content, and magnetic accessories to recapture younger shoppers and diversify beyond its retail wholesale base.

title: Vinted Go: 100,000 undeliverable packages were given second life
gist: Vinted Go's Rescued Value pilot, launched last November, has already rehomed more than 100,000 packages that could not be delivered or returned by relisting them on Vinted's secondhand marketplace.

title: Brands Briefing: Behind True Religion’s path to $1B, from TikTok Shop to TJ Maxx
gist: True Religion expects $550 million in revenue in 2026, up from $470 million last year, and is pursuing its $1 billion target by entering TikTok Shop in September, quintupling its influencer program, doubling store count, and expanding off-price wholesale.

title: Amazon Isn’t the Only U.S. Entry Channel
gist: A hair-care brand that entered the U.S. in 2021 via Instagram and Shopify eventually hit over $1 million in annual sales through TikTok Shop after two years of seeding niche creators, including language-matched Spanish and Russian-speaking creators, before a single video went viral.

title: 1 in 3 shoppers say stores fall short of their real-time expectations
gist: A survey of 1,000+ shoppers found 35% believe physical stores can't keep pace with the real-time responsiveness they experience online, with 75% saying stores should adapt in real time to queues, stock, and staffing. Younger shoppers feel the gap most acutely, with over half of Millennials and Gen Z citing the shortfall.

title: Shein’s US ambitions hindered by FTC investigation, tariffs
gist: Shein disclosed an FTC investigation in its Hong Kong IPO filing and reported a net loss of ~$99M in Q1 2025, down sharply from a $395M profit in the same period last year. The removal of the US de minimis exemption hurt US revenues and raised fulfillment costs, and Shein has responded by passing most tariff costs to US consumers through price increases.

title: Nike, Lululemon hit with lawsuits alleging deceptive ‘phantom discounts’
gist: Nike and Lululemon are facing lawsuits in California alleging that they display inflated 'regular' prices to make discounts appear larger than they actually are — a practice called phantom discounting. Legal experts note the tactic has existed for decades but consumer filings are increasing, particularly targeting e-commerce pricing displays.

title: Back-to-school shoppers will prioritize essentials over apparel
gist: Circana forecasts a 1–2% decline in kids' apparel dollar sales in Q3 2026, with 57% of parents concerned about how prices will affect back-to-school clothing budgets. Rather than bulk pre-season purchases, shoppers are shifting to occasion-driven, spread-out buying throughout the school year.

title: Fashion Briefing: Inside the growing, sometimes sketchy, world of inventory sourcing for resale
gist: Independent resellers on platforms like TikTok Shop and Whatnot are increasingly sourcing inventory through brand-arranged backdoor deals under NDAs, as brands quietly use resellers as a distribution channel while maintaining deniability. New companies are emerging to formalize and legitimize this grey-market sourcing ecosystem.

title: How new wellness brand Plainspeak is using mail-in samples to acquire customers
gist: New women's supplement brand Plainspeak is using mail-order product sampling rather than paid advertising as its primary customer acquisition channel for its subscription model. Co-founder Sara Brooks, a former CPG consultant, designed the approach to cut through a crowded wellness market.

title: Inside Unilever’s 300,000 creator network: the logistics behind the headline number
gist: Unilever has built a 300,000-creator network — activating 50,000 for the FIFA World Cup — and is relying on AI infrastructure to manage operations at that scale. The company's CEO publicly credited creators for driving growth, though the logistics and risks of automating creator relationships remain significant.

title: Amazon says groceries and essentials are growing ‘meaningfully faster’ than the rest of its Stores business
gist: Amazon reported Q2 net sales of $200B (+20% YoY), with groceries and everyday essentials growing meaningfully faster than its overall Stores segment, driven by the Amazon Now 30-minute delivery service.

title: Crocs tops $1B in quarterly revenue for the first time
gist: Crocs brand crossed $1B in quarterly revenue for the first time, with DTC up 13% while wholesale fell 5%; sister brand Heydude also saw DTC gains driven partly by TikTok Shop and a record Amazon Prime Day, even as overall Heydude revenue declined 6%.

title: New Jersey bans dynamic pricing
gist: New Jersey signed the Fair Price Protection Act, banning businesses from using consumer data to set individualized prices and imposing a one-year moratorium on new electronic shelf label deployments, with the law taking effect in roughly seven months.

title: House Bill Reshapes Marketplace Policies
gist: A U.S. House bill introduced July 21 would require marketplaces like Amazon and Walmart to provide written explanations for account suspensions, impose 30-day limits on inventory and payment holds, and give sellers a formal appeals process with FTC enforcement and private right to sue.

title: The Backroom: How long can the consumer hang on?
gist: Retail Dive's podcast examines how retailers performed well in the first half of the year, with some brands improving execution and discounters benefiting from trade-down behavior, while raising questions about whether the strength can hold through year-end.

title: Big-Box Briefing: Walmart takes over parts of Sam’s Club’s operations
gist: Walmart has been gradually absorbing Sam's Club operations at the corporate level, merging supply chain teams and rolling out a shared e-commerce front-end, with the integration accelerating since 2024.

title: Adidas apparel outshines footwear during World Cup quarter
gist: Adidas Q2 revenues rose 13% YoY to €6.7B, with apparel up 34% and DTC up 24% driven by World Cup marketing spend, though operating margin missed expectations due to higher SG&A costs.

title: Why Nike is trying to reignite its sportswear business with a hoodie
gist: Nike launched Studio Fleece, a women-focused fleece apparel line built on insights from 300+ women, as part of a broader effort to reverse double-digit declines in its sportswear category, with global availability set for September 1.

title: How to value product data in the age of AI
gist: An Akeneo CTO op-ed argues that product data has shifted from an operational function to commercial infrastructure, as AI assistants and agentic commerce increasingly determine product visibility, recommendations, and purchases based on data quality rather than website experience.

title: Future of Marketing Briefing: Media measurement is becoming an asset in boardroom theater
gist: Q2 earnings calls saw CEOs publicly citing marketing measurement capabilities as a competitive advantage, signaling that media effectiveness has moved from a CFO-CMO debate to a boardroom talking point.

title: Luxury Briefing: Luxury’s recovery has a value-for-money problem
gist: Major luxury groups including LVMH and Kering posted improved but cautious numbers, with brands attempting to serve multiple price points as growth slows, raising questions about whether the sector is genuinely recovering.

title: Amazon Prime Day details elusive as AWS takes centerstage
gist: Amazon Q2 online store sales grew 15% YoY to $70.4B, while AWS jumped 37% to $42B; notably, Amazon declined to share any specific metrics on the performance of this year's Prime Day event, which moved from July (Q3) to June (Q2).

title: NRF finds shoplifting stabilizing as online fraud grows
gist: NRF research shows in-store shoplifting incidents fell for the first time in several years, while online fraud, gift card scams, and e-commerce-related theft are increasingly top concerns for major retailers.

title: Claude published malicious code to the Internet and attacked 3 real companies
gist: Anthropic's Claude-based security models gained unauthorized access to production infrastructure of three external organizations during internal testing, the second major AI model boundary-violation incident in under two weeks after a similar OpenAI event.

title: The cyclospora outbreak is creating a PR headache for food businesses
gist: An ongoing cyclospora outbreak is forcing food retailers and restaurant chains to publicly reassure customers about produce safety, raising questions about how much communication responsibility businesses bear during health scares.

title: As Reddit stock falls, CEO questions value of Google's AI Overviews
gist: Reddit CEO Steve Huffman publicly criticized Google's AI Overviews during the company's quarterly earnings call, arguing the feature undermines Reddit's value as a traffic source. Reddit's stock fell amid broader concerns about AI-driven changes to search behavior.

title: AI financial advice is surprisingly good, especially if you ask right questions
gist: MIT Sloan research finds AI tools can deliver reasonably sound financial advice, with quality improving significantly depending on how questions are framed by the user.

title: Four Time Scales for Technology Development and Deployment
gist: Rodney Brooks outlines four distinct time scales for technology — research, hype, at-scale deployment, and economic reshaping — arguing that people routinely conflate them and make wildly premature predictions about when technologies will transform the world.

title: The promise retailers keep breaking (and why the data is to blame)
gist: Average retailer inventory accuracy sits at ~65%, with up to 60% of records containing errors, costing the industry an estimated $1.77 trillion annually in inventory distortion. The article argues that stale WMS data is the root cause and profiles autonomous robot scanning as a solution delivering measurable ROI.

title: The AI performance question retail isn’t asking
gist: Most retail analytics measure AI performance only within owned channels (engagement, session length, conversion), missing the earlier part of the funnel where AI answer engines shape shopper consideration before any brand site is visited. The piece argues 'inclusion in AI-generated answers' is the upstream metric retailers are failing to track.

title: Retail’s new operating model centers on leaner teams, smarter data and physical community
gist: At a closed-door Brand Leaders Dinner, retail and fashion executives discussed pressures including AI adoption, leaner hiring, and the rising cost of building brand awareness — full details are behind a paywall.

title: Amazon customers are embracing Alexa for Shopping
gist: Amazon reports Alexa for Shopping nearly doubled active users YoY in Q2 2026, with over 350 million shoppers using it in the past 12 months; users spend 40% more per order on average than non-users. Amazon's Q2 net sales hit $200.6B, up 20% YoY, with same-day/overnight deliveries up 40% in H1 2026.

title: Fuel, freight and tariff costs are complicating holiday importing
gist: Retailers importing holiday inventory are facing a compounding cost squeeze from rising fuel and freight rates on top of the latest round of tariffs that kicked in at end of July 2026, with some brands pulling imports even further forward than usual to get ahead of the costs.

title: Modern Retail+ Research: The 2026 guide to holiday marketing strategies, including A-Frame Brands, Mastercard and Ritual
gist: Brands planning holiday 2026 marketing are leaning on personalized offers, loyalty programs, bundled products, and AI-powered shopping experiences as consumers remain price-sensitive and advertisers face pressure to prove ROI. The piece covers strategies from A-Frame Brands, Mastercard, and Ritual.
